capabilityReferences.use: Proposed latest-version capability names only, not historical availability or proof that every node supports them.
io_uring and static-binary/uprobe blind spots; no blanket complete-observation assumption.
Current hardware-source/CPU-time proportional attribution, boundaries and limitations.
Historical energy interfaces; do not conflate legacy model fallback and current RAPL architecture.

executionGates: Research-only: do not load into the existing 100-plan builder, scored roster or reproduction runner.

Verify exact source version, node image, OS, architecture, kernel/BTF, cgroup mode, runtime and managed support before any attempt; unavailable historical prerequisites are blocked, not silently replaced.
First establish a bounded fault trigger, independent oracle and healthy/recovery control. Intermittent, rare, high-scale and adapted designs remain conditional.
Review current comments/fixes and linked reproductions before implementation; closed issue state alone is not proof of a fix.
Use owned isolated resources, predeclared resource/time/cost caps, stop conditions, cleanup ownership and cleanup verification. Cloud and model costs need separate authorization.
Trace only synthetic scoped workloads with least privileges. Avoid packet payloads, secret/token contents and arbitrary command lines; redact addresses and identifiers.
Treat unsupported collection, incomplete streams, missing usage, stale counters and unknown sensor availability explicitly; never turn them into zero, healthy, or a completed experiment.
Compare Kubernetes-only and augmented evidence on the same bounded experiment without answer repair, score retries or changing the oracle after seeing model output.

For energy, record measured host/domain versus modelled source versus estimated workload allocation versus utilization/cost proxy. Do not claim carbon reduction without energy and an explicit time/location factor.

baseline: Pod/node status and events
Volume and workload configuration
Application timing and offered load
additional: Per-device latency, queue depth and byte/operation counters
Process/file I/O attribution
Azure disk/SKU/cache limits and actual node tuning
io.caveat: Node block I/O is not remote storage service latency. io_uring paths can bypass syscall-based file gadgets; retain application/provider metrics.

baseline: Requests/limits, scheduling, events and probe definitions
Pod/node resource metrics with collection timestamps
additional: cgroup CPU time and throttling counters
Work completed and latency at fixed load
Process CPU profiles or Windows performance counters
cpu.caveat: A request is not a limit; throttled-period ratio is not necessarily lost throughput or an outage. CPU time is not energy.

baseline: Restart/termination reason, memory limits and node pressure
Workload and mount inventory
additional: OOM victim/cgroup identity
RSS/cache/working-set accounting over time
Kernel/runtime diagnostics and workload cardinality
memory.caveat: A memory request below usage is not evidence of a leak. Pin the cgroup accounting model and OOM observation support.

baseline: Services, endpoints, node placement and events
Workload/application errors and connection timing
additional: Connection tuples and directional counters without payload
Routes, neighbors, conntrack, HNS or BPF state
Provider LB/NSG/flow telemetry when the proposed attribution crosses the node boundary
network.caveat: Linux Gadget is not a Windows tracer. TCP gadgets do not observe ARP or UDP; use bounded header-only captures for those protocols.

baseline: Pod dnsPolicy/dnsConfig, Service/endpoints and resolver logs
Collector/application failing target and timestamp
additional: DNS query/response timing and return code for the actual destination
Host/custom resolver configuration and fallback path
dns.caveat: Record search expansion and resolver implementation. Redact names and validate duration units, filters and collection loss.

baseline: Client/controller logs and request settings
API events and available server metrics
additional: Client limiter, DNS/connect/response timing
Authorized audit/managed diagnostic logs with caller identity
Known workload request rates
api.caveat: Node-level tracing cannot reveal unseen managed-control-plane callers or prove the source of server-side saturation.

baseline: Pod scheduling events and effective requests
NodeClaims, nodes, taints, affinity and autoscaler decisions
additional: ARM provisioning state and SKU/capacity constraints
Timeline of upcoming/replaced/idle nodes and workload completion
scheduling.caveat: Kubernetes evidence often suffices for proximate scheduling diagnosis; kernel tracing does not establish Azure regional capacity.

baseline: Image/platform, manifest, events, restart and object ownership state
Controller and kubelet logs where accessible
additional: ARM operation status and boot/CSE diagnostics
Runtime response timings, registry manifests and provider build logs
lifecycle.caveat: Do not infer current managed behavior from historical versions; unavailable historical images block exact reproduction.

baseline: Service-account, Role/Binding and authorization errors
Redacted kubeconfig/schema and projected identity metadata
additional: ARM/Entra scope and propagation evidence
Credential-path metadata without tokens or secret values
identity.caveat: Kubernetes RBAC and ARM/Entra authorization are different. Do not trace secret payloads or retain tokens.

baseline: PVC/PV/VolumeAttachment/VolumeSnapshot states and CSI logs
Mount options, workload lifecycle and timeout events
additional: Provider resource inventory and timestamped operations
Node mount/session state and filesystem timings
Windows SMB diagnostics where applicable
storage.caveat: Provider completion, Kubernetes reconciliation and node filesystem readiness are separate. Gadgets cannot identify server-side Azure Files causes alone.

baseline: All applicable policy selectors and pod identities
Endpoint/Service/node objects and controller logs
additional: Effective iptables/ipset/BPF enforcement state
Bounded allow/deny traffic matrix and drop evidence
policy.caveat: NetworkPolicy is additive. API object state is not proof of actual enforcement, and kernel drop-reason decoding must be validated.

baseline: Requested/allocatable device resources, images and device-plugin events
Driver feature validation and workload timing
additional: Loaded module/userspace version, NVML/DCGM counters and supported sensor domains
GPU process activity, clock/error state and per-iteration timing
gpu.caveat: GPU gadgets are proposed latest-version capabilities, not verified on the historical source. Utilization and starvation are not measured GPU energy.

baseline: Independent workload lifecycle and known event counts
Collector image, configuration, logs and termination status
additional: Kernel/BTF, runtime socket, cgroup mode and permission matrix
Raw events, field validity, lost-event counters and stream completion
Independent runtime inventory or bounded reference capture
tracing.caveat: Gadget is the subject under test here. Its own output cannot be the sole ground truth for missing events, identity, order or drop reasons.

baseline: Exporter deployment/health, workload identity and resource configuration
Metric names, labels, type, units, timestamps and scrape outcome
additional: Explicit sensor/model source and measurement boundary
Raw cumulative energy or power with sampling intervals and reset handling
Synchronized independent hardware reference when available; otherwise uncertainty
energy.caveat: Inspektor Gadget is workload context only, not an energy meter. Workload energy attribution is estimated even when the host counter is hardware-derived.
